jia: quick heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-selection rollout we saw a big drop in prefix cache hit rate for chat-like traffic, digging in now
ant: which metric moved first? hit-rate, latency, or cost?
maria: hit-rate. numbers from last 24h vs baseline: prefix hit-rate went 78% -> 52%, p95 latency +12ms, avg token cost +7% (inferred from token count and GPU time)
jia: confirmed. profiler shows KV cache miss spike aligned with rollout window. sample KV miss log lines: `kv_cache::miss model=v1.3.0 kernel=auto-select seq=64 prefix_key=...`
olga: interesting — did the key synthesis change? we only touched kernel selection but the new code path pulls `normalized_input` from the tokenizer wrapper, which now returns different spacing for function args
ant: that could explain it. small changes in spacing/json ordering break keys. do we have an example mismatch?
maria: yes — here are two keys for the same user prompt (redacted):
```
sha1(\"system:You are an assistant|user:Summarize the text:  ...\") = a1f5...
sha1(\"system:You are an assistant\nuser:Summarize the text:\t...\") = b7e2...
```
keys differ because of newline vs space and a tab in the second serialization
jia: ugh. the new tokenizer wrapper normalizes unicode but preserves original whitespace in some cases. kernel auto-select route calls `tokenizer.serialize()` instead of `tokenizer.canonicalize()` — my bad, missed the pinning step
perf-bot: alert — cache_miss_rate (+38%) detected for route `/v1/chat/generate` between 2026-03-17T03:12Z and 2026-03-17T04:10Z
maria: short-term mitigation: we can fallback to old key synthesis in the serving runtime for any requests that came through the `auto-select` kernel until we push a fix. that should restore ~24% of hit-rate immediately
ant: longer-term: we need deterministic key components: (1) normalized system prompt (strip extra whitespace, stable newline canonical), (2) normalized user prompt (unicode NFC, trim repeated whitespace), (3) deterministic ordering for `tools`/`functions` fields, (4) explicit tokenizer version tag in the key. also add `key_version` so we can evolve it safe-ly
olga: +1 on deterministic tools ordering. most callers send tools as JSON lists and insertion order varies between client libs. propose we sort by `name` then by `schema` hash before serializing
jia: proposing code stub for synth key (will paste to repo):
```
def synth_key(system, user, tools, tokenizer_tag, key_version="v1"):
    s = normalize_text(system)
    u = normalize_text(user)
    t = serialize_tools(sorted_tools(tools))
    payload = key_version + '|' + tokenizer_tag + '|' + s + '|' + u + '|' + t
    return sha1(payload)
```
ant: also: pin tokenizer_tag = f"{model}@{tokenizer_version}". we already have tokenizer version in the model metadata store, let's thread it through the serving path rather than re-querying during hot path
maria: warmup strategy: run a nightly prefetch job that replays the top-200k prefixes (by frequency) to populate KV on all serving pools. we have a bucketed list from logs (freq_by_prefix_{date}.parquet)
jia: note — warmup needs to use the same synth key code as runtime. otherwise we'll prefill wrong keys. so deploy synth_key change to both warmup job and runtime in same release window
olga: regression root cause summarized: kernel-selection change pulled a different tokenizer serialization which changed whitespace -> cache key divergence -> reduced prefix hits -> higher latency/cost. fix plan: revert kernel change OR add compatibility shim + rollout key-version bump + warmup prefill
perf-bot: perf regression ticket created: PERF-4829 (root cause: cache key divergence after kernel-select rollout)
deploy-bot: deploy logged — rollback flagged for hotfix branch, author=jia, pr=gh/infra/444
jia: I'm going to open the PR that: (a) adds deterministic tools ordering, (b) pins tokenizer_tag in runtime metadata, (c) updates synth_key function, (d) adds a migration job that backfills keys for last 30 days of top prefixes. will tag olga+ant for review
ant: assign owners and ETA?
olga: can do review today, can approve if tests pass. ETA for hotfix release ~2-3 hours after PR merged (we need a quick canary then full rollout)
maria: post-mortem todo: add metric `cache_key_entropy` and an alert if it jumps >10% relative to baseline, and add unit tests verifying stable key output for a set of canonical inputs (including weird whitespace/unicode/tool ordering)
jia: thanks all. I'll update PERF-4829 with numbers and link to PR. action items pinned in the ticket: `jia` fix+PR, `olga` review, `ant` validate warmup job, `maria` follow up on metrics/alerts
ant: one more thought — batching heuristics: if we have lower hit-rate we should temporarily tighten batch size rampdown to favor latency (fewer tokens wasted on misses). I'll open a small runtime config change to lower max_batch_size from 64 -> 48 for `/v1/chat/*` during the hotfix window
jia: small typo in the last message (should be jia) — noted.
olga: :thumbsup:
maria: re-check will run after hotfix, and we expect prefix hit-rate to recover to ~75% after warmup and deterministic key rollout
jia: thanks team, updating ticket now
